questions.prompt: According to the ordinance, where is it lawful for someone to drink or have in open possession liquor on a street, alley, or other public place?
choices: Any street or public building without restriction.
Only on city-owned streets or leased premises with an ABC license in the Arts and Entertainment District.
Only if you pay a fee to city hall first.
It is never lawful regardless of location.
questions.answer: Only on city-owned streets or leased premises with an ABC license in the Arts and Entertainment District.
questions.excerpt:
Footnotes: --- ( 1 ) --- Cross reference— Businesses, ch. 22. State Law reference— Alcoholic beverages, Code of Ala. 1975, § 28-1-1 et seq.

(a) It shall be unlawful for any person to drink or have in open or unconcealed possession,
               or custody, for drinking, selling, serving, dispensing, or give away; or attempting
               to drink, sell, serve, dispense, or give away, any liquor, wine or malt brewed beverages,
               while upon any street, avenue, or alley, or in any public building or upon any property,
               or while in any other public place in the city. As used in this section, the term
               "public place" shall mean and include any place or gathering which the public generally
               attends or is admitted to either by invitations, common consent or right, or by payment
               of an admission or other charge, and, without limited the generality of the foregoing,
               shall include any theatre or other place of amusement and any contest; provided that
               such term shall not include city owned streets or leased premises which are a part
               of the Arts and Entertainment District pursuant to Ordinance No. 2015-11 or city owned
               premises leased to a person or entity which has an ABC license to distribute alcoholic
               beverages. (b) This section shall not apply to persons in open possession of the above described
               alcoholic beverages during a special event and within the parameters and time of the
               special event as defined in the application of such special event in accordance with sections 22-41 through 22-43 of this Code. (Ord. No. 1012, § 1, 7-18-1994; Ord. questions.prompt: How many citizens make up the park and recreation board?
questions.answer: Nine
questions.excerpt:
Footnotes: --- ( 1 ) --- Cross reference— Park and street tree committee, § 19-21 et seq.; land use and development ordinance, App. A. State Law reference— Powers of city, Code of Ala. 1975, § 11-47-211 et seq.

Under the authority of Section 11-86-1 of the Code of Alabama 1975, as amended, there
               is hereby created the park and recreation board of the City of Bay Minette, Alabama.
               Such board is to have charge of the operation and maintenance of all parks and recreation
               areas of the city. The board shall consist of nine citizens of the city, who shall
               be chosen because of their civic interests and who shall be persons particularly interested
               in the development of city athletic facilities, city parks and city playgrounds. Said
               board members shall serve without compensation. Members of the board shall be selected
               and appointed by the city council of the city. (Ord. No. 777, § 1, 10-21-86)

The original members of the board shall serve for terms of one, two, three, four and
               five years, respectively, from October, 1986, and the successors to the original members
               of the board shall serve for terms of five years. Vacancies and unexpired terms shall
               be filled in the same manner as original appointments are made. At a meeting of the
               city council in October of each year the city council shall elect a successor to the
               member(s) of the board whose term(s) expire(s) during that year and successor(s) shall
               take office immediately and serve for a term of five years. (Ord. No. 777, § 2, 10-21-86)

questions.excerpt:
The purpose of this article shall be to coordinate the type, placement, and physical
               dimensions of signs within the city; to recognize the commercial communication requirements
               of all sectors of the business community; to encourage the innovative use of design;
               to promote both renovation and proper maintenance; to allow for special circumstances;
               and to guarantee equal treatment under the law through accurate record keeping and
               consistent enforcement. These shall be accomplished by regulation of the display,
               erection, use and maintenance of signs. The placement and physical dimensions of signs
               are regulated primarily by type and length of street frontage. No sign shall be permitted
               as a main or accessory use except in accordance with the provisions of this article.
               The city council finds and declares that it is a valid public purpose to enact this
               article to promote the governmental interests of aesthetics and public safety for
               the city. (Code 1979, § 2.5-21; Ord. No. 5-1-90, § 1(1.01), 5-15-1990)

This article shall not relate to building design, nor shall this article regulate
               official traffic or government signs; the copy and message of signs; window displays;
               product dispensers and point of purchase displays; scoreboards on athletic fields;
               flags of any nation, government, or noncommercial organization; gravestones; barber
               poles; religious symbols; commemorative plaques; the display of street numbers; or
               any display or construction not defined herein as a sign. (Code 1979, § 2.5-22; Ord. No. 5-1-90, § 1(1.02), 5-15-1990)

               Code of Ala. 1975, § 28-3A-21; general authority as to regulation of liquors and beverages,

It shall be unlawful for any person, firm or corporation licensed to sell alcoholic
               beverages to sell, give away or otherwise dispose of or serve for consumption alcoholic

questions.prompt: If you drive to Hurricane Park to use the playground, picnic tables, or ball fields, how should you park?
choices: Enter through the main gate and park in the parking lot
Park in the spaces by the tennis courts
questions.answer: Enter through the main gate and park in the parking lot
questions.excerpt:
Footnotes: --- ( 1 ) --- State Law reference— Municipal parks, playgrounds and other recreational and athletic areas and facilities,
               Code of Ala. 1975, § 11-47-210 et seq.

(a) Parking lot use. Patrons of Hurricane Park, for other than the tennis courts and caboose, will enter
               all motorized vehicles through the main gate and park in the parking lot. This applies
               for everyone using the ball fields, basketball courts, playground, picnic tables,
               lake, jogging and walking trail and other features that may be added to the park in
               the future. (b) Tennis court parking. There are a limited number of parking spaces by the tennis courts that should normally
               accommodate those persons using the courts or visiting the caboose. (c) Exceptions. The following is a list of exceptions to the vehicular restrictions: (1) Park maintenance vehicles and equipment. (2) Vehicles delivering handicapped persons. (3) Motorized wheelchairs. (4) Contractor vehicles and equipment hired by the town. (d) Penalty for violation of section. Violation of this section will constitute a misdemeanor and will be subject to section 1-9 . (Code 1999, § 50-1; Ord. No. 261, §§ 1—4, 3-25-1991)

(a) General prohibition; town liability. Swimming in the Hurricane Park Lake is prohibited and the town will not be responsible
               for accidents resulting from any such activity. (b) Posting of signs. The town clerk will cause signs to be posted at the lake to remind the public that
               swimming is prohibited. (c) Erection and placement of signs. The superintendent will see that the signs are erected in a permanent manner in the
               best locations for viewing by the public. (Code 1999, § 50-2; Ord. No. 262, §§ 1—3, 3-25-1991)

The city council has adopted the state highway department standards for accommodating
               utilities on highway rights-of-way as standards for use by the city for accommodating
               utilities on roads and streets under the jurisdiction of the city on those roads and
               streets which have or will involve the expenditure of state or federal highway funds. (Code 1988, § 18-1; Ord. of 10-19-1971, § 1)

It is unlawful for any person to obstruct a street or sidewalk with goods or merchandise,
               lumber or fuel or any article or obstruction whatever, except under permit from the
               city. (Code 1962, § 16-1; Code 1988, § 18-2)

(a) No person shall place advertising materials, including signs, temporary or non-temporary,
               in or on city rights-of-way or city-owned property. Prohibited materials include,
               but are not limited to, political advertising, yard sale notices, and any sign promoting
               a private use, except that businesses can rent the DeKalb Theater marquee to promote
               their enterprise. Directional signs for government, schools, or charitable agency
               buildings are specifically excluded from this provision. (b) If right-of-way boundaries cannot be easily determined, citizens may contact the public
               works department of the city for assistance. In any case, the above-described prohibited
               signs must be placed a minimum of 15 feet from the street pavement or established
               roadbed for the safety of the traveling public. (c) Violations of this section constitute misdemeanors punishable, upon conviction, by
               a fine of not less than $1.00 nor more than $500.00 or be imprisoned in the city jail
               for a period not to exceed six months, or both such fine and imprisonment. (Ord. No. 2004-18, 12-21-2004; Ord. No. 2021-01, 1-19-2021)

questions.prompt: Montevallo treats the city cemetery as closed after it is too dark for an ordinarily-sighted person to:
choices: Read a newspaper without extra light
Walk the paths without a flashlight
questions.answer: Read a newspaper without extra light
questions.excerpt:
Without the permission of the city clerk, it shall be unlawful to enter or remain
               in the city cemetery between dusk and dawn, which is defined as any time that it is
               so dark that an ordinarily-sighted person cannot read a newspaper without the aid
               of artificial or lunar illumination. The city clerk may establish and close gates
               on the cemetery streets in aid of the enforcement of this section. (Code 1982, § 4-25; Ord. No. 94J, § 4-25, 1-23-1995)

It shall be unlawful for any person, firm, or corporation to tear up or disturb for
               any purpose the surface of any sidewalk, street, alley, or other public place, without
               first obtaining a permit to do so from the city clerk. All such work shall be done
               under the direct supervision and control of said clerk. (Code 1980; Code 1982, § 4-62)

It shall be unlawful to promote, organize, hold, or assist in organizing or holding,
               or to take part in, any parade, funeral procession, or other public demonstration
               in the streets or other public ways of the city, unless in accordance with the terms
               of a permit therefor, secured from the city clerk or the city council. To secure such
               permit, written application shall be made to the city clerk setting forth the hour
               and date, the probable number of persons, vehicles, and animals which will be engaged
               in such parade, procession, or other public demonstration, and the streets or other
               public ways which may be used therefor, unless in their judgment the public convenience,
               health, peace, safety, or welfare require that it be refused. Deviating from the permitted
               route or time is unlawful. (Code 1982, § 4-120; Ord. of 6-25-1963)

               city without the consent…

questions.prompt: What exact sign must a Moody tavern, lounge, night club, or saloon owner post where people can see it?
choices: NO ONE UNDER 21 ALLOWED TO DRINK
PERSONS UNDER THE AGE OF 21 YEARS NOT ALLOWED HERE
questions.answer: PERSONS UNDER THE AGE OF 21 YEARS NOT ALLOWED HERE
questions.excerpt:
Footnotes: --- ( 1 ) --- State Law reference— Alcoholic beverages, Code of Ala. 1975, § 28-1-1 et seq.; Alcoholic Beverage Licensing
               Code, Code of Ala. 1975, § 28-3A-1 et seq.

               or keeper of a tavern, lounge, night club, saloon or other similarly situated business,
               shall employ or permit any person under the age of 21 years to frequent or be in or
               about such place, or to drink any intoxicating liquors or beer or any other fermented
               malt beverage or alcoholic beverage in or about the same, or for any person, regardless
               of age, to bet or wager on any game of billiards, or other game, to bet or wager with
               any cards or any other gambling device, or any other game whatsoever, in or about
               such place. (b) It shall be the duty of any person who is the proprietor or keeper of a tavern, lounge,
               night club, saloon or other similarly situated business to post conspicuously in his
               place of business the following sign: "PERSONS UNDER THE AGE OF 21 YEARS NOT ALLOWED HERE" (Ord. No. M1988-09-26, 9-26-1988)

questions.prompt: Unless a sign says otherwise, what’s the speed limit for cars, trucks, and motorcycles on streets in Moundville?
choices: The same as nearby county roads
questions.answer: 30 miles per hour
questions.excerpt:
Footnotes: --- ( 1 ) --- State Law reference— Traffic generally, Code of Ala. 1975, § 32-5-1 et seq.; rules of the road, Code of
               Ala. 1975, § 32-5A-1 et seq.; powers of local authorities, Code of Ala. 1975, § 32-5-1.

Unless otherwise posted, the maximum speed that an automobile, truck, tractor, motorcycle
               or other motor-driven vehicle may be driven or operated on any street, highway or
               thoroughfare in the corporate limits shall be 30 miles per hour. However, the city
               council may from time to time establish greater or lesser limits in school zones,
               in areas of congestion and in areas where the mayor and council deem the operation
               at 30 miles per hour to be dangerous to life, limb and property or in areas where
               a greater speed is authorized as a result of traffic and road conditions. When such
               greater or lesser limits are established, the city council shall adopt a resolution
               to that effect and shall cause signs to be erected warning the public of the differing
               speed restriction.

Speed limits as described in section 22-1 shall apply so long as the city limits remain as they are on the date of the adoption
               of the ordinance from which this chapter is derived. In the event they are extended,
               this chapter shall be revised to properly cover the new territory. (Ord. No. 2013-05, § VI, 8-26-2013)

In addition to all provisions of law relating to the speed and operation of motor
               vehicles in the city, there are hereby adopted by the city all laws of the state and
               all rules and regulations of the state department of transportation pertaining to
               control of traffic and motor vehicles on highways, that are misdemeanors under the
               state laws and violations of such laws, rules, and regulations in the city, or in
               the police…

This chapter shall be known and may be cited as the "New Hope Alcoholic Beverage Ordinance." (Ord. No. 401, § 1.01, 7-10-2017)

The ordinance from which this chapter is derived is enacted for the purposes, among
               others, of promoting the health and general welfare of the community, of establishing
               reasonable standards for the regulation and control of the licensing and sales of
               alcoholic beverages, and of protecting and preserving the nature and character of
               the city. It is the intent of the council in enacting the ordinance from which this
               chapter is derived to advance these purposes by giving reasonable consideration to
               the character of various areas of the city and their peculiar suitability for particular
               uses, to the congestion in the streets and roads of the city, to promoting desirable
               living conditions and sustaining stability of neighborhoods and property values, and
               to the discouragement and prevention of abuse of alcoholic beverages and inappropriate
               or illegal conduct resulting from such abuse. This chapter shall be construed as an
               exercise by the city of its police power as delegated to it by the Code of Alabama
               for the regulation of traffic in alcoholic beverages within the city. (Ord. No. 401, § 1.02, 7-10-2017)

questions.prompt: What is the entire city of Oneonta designated as?
questions.answer: A bird sanctuary
questions.excerpt:
Footnotes: --- ( 1 ) --- Cross reference— Dead animal disposal, § 24-41.

The entire area embraced within the corporate limits of the city is designated as
               a bird sanctuary. (Ord. No. B-20, 2-8-72)

(a) Unlawful. It shall be unlawful to trap, hunt, shoot or attempt to shoot or molest in any manner
               any bird or wild fowl or to rob bird nests or wild fowl nests. However, if starlings
               or similar birds are found to be congregating in a particular locality in such numbers
               that they constitute a nuisance or menace to health or property in the opinion of
               the proper health authorities of the city, then the health authorities shall meet
               with representatives of the Audubon Society, Bird Club, Garden Club or Humane Society,
               or as many of those clubs as are found to exist in the city, after having given clubs
               at least three (3) days' actual notice of the time and place of the meeting to the
               representatives of the clubs. (b) Nuisance birds. If as a result of the meeting no satisfactory alternative is found to abate such nuisance,
               then the birds may be destroyed in such numbers and in such manner as is deemed advisable
               by the health authorities under supervision of the chief of police of the city. (c) Penalty. Anyone violating the provisions of this section shall be punished as provided in section 1-8 . (Ord. No. B-20, 2-8-72) Cross reference— Discharge of firearms, generally, § 16-3 .

               violating this section shall be guilty of a misdemeanor and upon conviction thereof
               shall be punished as provided in section 1-8…

questions.answer: A bird sanctuary
questions.excerpt:
Footnotes: --- ( 1 ) --- Cross reference— Creation of noise by animals, § 8-3(b)(7); removal of dead animals, §§ 9-82, 9-87.

For the purposes of this chapter, the following terms shall have the meanings respectively
               ascribed to them: Animal. Any male or female dog, pet fox, wolf or other member of the canine family, or member
               of the feline (cat) family; provided that no such animal shall be deemed to be a dog
               within the terms of this chapter unless it is at least three (3) months old. At large. Unrestrained and not under the control of the owner or other person acting for the
               owner, such control to be exercised either: (1) by confinement within a fence, wall
               or other enclosure in such a manner as to effectively prevent the escape of the animal;
               or (2) by the restraint of the animal by a leash, cord or chain not less than ten
               (10) feet in length and secured to a collar, with swivel connections, in such a manner
               as to effectively prevent the escape of the animal; provided, however, that the length
               of the leash, cord or chain shall be reduced to such length as to prevent the animal,
               when so secured, from entering premises other than that of the owner; (3) when the
               animal is in a public place and off the premises of the owner by the restraint of

questions.prompt: In Pelham, when does an electronic fence count as confining a dog so it is not at large?

Whenever the fence is installed around the yard
Only if a neighbor agrees in writing
Never; dogs must always be on a leash
questions.answer: When the fence is activated and working and the dog wears a working receiver
questions.excerpt:
For the purpose of this chapter, the following terms shall have the meanings respectively
               ascribed to them: At large : A dog or other animal shall be deemed to be at large when it is not under restraint
               by its owner or a competent person having charge or control of it or when it is not
               confined within a wall, fence, vehicle or other enclosure in such manner as to effectively
               prevent it from escape, including an electronic fence which is activated and in good
               working order and is used in connection with an effective and working receiver attached
               to each dog or other animal which is confined thereby and which effectively prevents
               it from escape. Dog : Either a male or female dog, and shall include pet foxes, wolves and other members
               of the canine family; provided that no such animal shall be deemed to be a dog within
               the terms of this chapter unless it is three or more months old. Dog control center : Any premises designated by the city or the county health department for the purposes
               of impounding and caring for animals. Kennel: The premises of any person engaged in the business of breeding, buying, selling or

               animal in such person's care or acts as its custodian or permits it to remain on or
               about the premises occupied by such person. Rabies control officer : The person employed by the city or the county health department to assist the supervisor

               by a leash, cord, chain…

This chapter shall be known and may be cited as the "Russellville Alcoholic Beverage
               Ordinance." (Ord. No. 2011-101, § 1, 1-24-11)

This chapter is enacted for the purposes, among others, of promoting the health and
               general welfare of the community, of establishing reasonable standards for the regulation
               and control of the licensing and sales of alcoholic beverages, and of protecting and
               preserving certain areas, through reasonable consideration, among others, to the character
               of the areas and their peculiar suitability for particular uses, to the congestion
               in the roads and streets, to a general view of promoting desirable living conditions
               and sustaining stability of neighborhoods and property values, and to the prevention
               of undesirable persons from engaging in or having any interest in alcoholic beverages.
               This chapter shall be construed as an exercise by the city of the police power of
               the state delegate to the city, in the regulation of traffic in alcoholic beverages
               within the city as provided by state law. (Ord. No. 2011-101, § 2, 1-24-11)

               are hereby adopted by reference, and made a part hereof as if fully set forth herein
               unless otherwise modified herein. In addition thereto, the following terms shall have
               the meanings herein specifically ascribed to them: Alcoholic beverage means any alcoholic, spirituous, vinous, fermented or other alcoholic beverage, or
               combination of liquors and mixed liquor, a part of which is spirituous, vinous, fermented
               or otherwise alcoholic, and all drinks or drinkable liquids, preparations or mixtures
               intended for beverage purposes, which contain one-half of one percent or more of alcohol

questions.prompt: What is the official name of Tuscaloosa's rules for mobile home parks?
questions.answer: Tuscaloosa Mobile Home Park Ordinance
questions.excerpt:
Footnotes: --- ( 1 ) --- Cross reference— Business regulations, Ch. 7; flood damage regulations, §§ 6-97—6-99. Zoning reference—Restriction on parking mobile home outside of park, zoning ordinance, § 35-38.

This chapter shall be known and may be cited as the "Tuscaloosa Mobile Home Park Ordinance." (Code 1962, § 21A-1)

(a) The governing body finds that properly designed and operated mobile home parks: (1) Promote the safety and health of the residents of such parks, and (2) Provide a suitable and much needed accommodation for an increasingly popular variety
               of housing. (b) It is, therefore, declared to be the policy of this city to eliminate and prevent
               health and safety hazards and to promote the economical and orderly development and
               utilization of land by providing for planning and operating mobile home parks and
               by providing for the standards and regulations necessary to accomplish these purposes. (Code 1962, § 21A-2)

For purposes of this chapter, the following terms shall have the respective meanings
               ascribed to them: Accessory structure: Any structural addition to the mobile home which includes awnings, cabanas, carports,
               Florida rooms, porches, ramadas, storage cabinets and similar appurtenant structures. Building: A roofed structure erected for permanent use. Building official: The chief building official. Common area: Any area or space designed for joint use of tenants occupying mobile home parks. Community system (water or sewerage): A central system which serves all living units and is not publicly owned. Density: The number of mobile homes or mobile home stands per gross acre. Driveway: A minor private way used by vehicles and pedestrians on a mobile home lot or for
               common access to a small group of lots or common facilities. Dwelling: Same as "Living unit." Easement: A vested or acquired right to use land, other than as tenant, for a specific…
